messages.author: 8fbb292485019894
messages.subject: multiplicities in STAN
parts:
Quick question ...

In the HMC STAN uses, there is a Metropolis-Hastings acceptance criteria applied to new proposal points.  Normally, if rejected, the current point is repeated in the M-H acceptance algorithm.  Usually, this is specified by assigning a multiplicity to the points -- e.g. the number of times a point is repeated.  In the STAN output (via the "extract()" member method in pystan) there seems to be neither multiplicity values nor are points repeated in the chain.  I'm confused why multiplicities are not specified ... Could you please explain? -- Thank you.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multiplicities in STAN
parts:
There's no Metropolis step in NUTS. See the Hoffman
and Gelman JMLR paper.

In basic HMC, if you simulate the Hamiltonian accurately, the
acceptance probability is 100%, but that's not usually
a good tradeoff for speed (because you need a low step
size).

In either algorithm, you can get repeated draws.

Just dumping out all the draws is more conventional in
my experience, as it feeds more neatly into things like
the autocorrelation algorithm we use for computing effective
sample size. We could do counts when there are repeats, but
then we'd have to change all of our downstream algorithms.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multiplicities in STAN
parts:
I have never seen a Metropolis-Hastings algorithm specified
by such a multiplicity so I can’t claim that I fully understand
your question.  Almost every Metropolis-Hastings algorithm
coming out of statistics is specified by the average acceptance
probability.

The NUTS sampler in Stan is more subtle as it’s not a
straightforward Metropolis-Hastings algorithm.  Instead of
trying to jump to just one point we try to jump to all points
in the trajectory, and when those trajectories are nontrivially
long the probability of staying at the initial point is very small.
Of course this is what you want, as many repeats of a single
state indicate very low acceptance probabilities and hence
very large autocorrelations.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multiplicities in STAN
parts:
I think he meant that rather than repeating draws in the
output, you'd just record how many times each one was seen.
That can be more compact and more efficient for calculating
expectations, especially if the number of repeats is high
compared to the number of parameters.

- Bob
